summary: Weekly POC sync focusing on an incident during Thursday's peak when several requests hit timeouts and 5xx errors. Team triaged root causes to a combination of aggressive client retries, token-throttling at upstream rate-limiter, and an unexpected KV cache miss storm. Agreed on immediate mitigations (soft rate-limits, exponential backoff tuning, temporary dedicated burst) and next steps to run larger scale retry simulations, update dashboards, and schedule a canary region fallback test.
transcript:
Header: Date/Time: 2025-07-09 15:00 UTC
Duration: 46m
Meeting link: https://meet.redwood.example/abc123 (recording attached)
Attendees: Sofia Martinez (Redwood AE), Devon Park (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (TerraScale), Ethan Liu (TerraScale SRE), Marco Hernandez (TerraScale CTO)
Shared artifacts: postmortem doc + sim sheet: https://redwood.example.com/poc/TS/retry-backoff.xlsx; security packet: https://redwood.example.com/sec/TS-pkg.pdf

Summary (auto): quick recap of Thursday incident; primary action is sim + parameter tuning; discuss Dedicated burst option.

[00:00] Sofia: Hey everybody, thanks for joining, I know we're short on time so we'll run the postmortem and next steps. Devon and I will do the tech bits, Priya/Ethan you can jump in with the traffic sample and questions.
[00:18] Priya: yep, thanks - we got clobbered on Thu around 14:32 UTC, our payment inference lane saw a spike, lots of timeouts and then a handful of 5xx returned from the Redwood API. We had clients retrying aggressively.
[00:31] Devon: right, initial look shows two things: client-side retry storms plus the upstream token-bucket hitting its hard-limit. Also saw a KV cache miss cascade - when cache warmed off we had high p99 latencies.
[00:48] Ethan: quick clarification - the 5xx were from Redwood or from our edge? We saw 502s in our proxy logs and a few 503s from the endpoint.
[01:04] Devon: most 5xx correlate with request ids where Redwood returned 5xx at the model-proxy layer; some were retries after a timeout that triggered our rate-limiter fallback. Logs attached in the sheet, though some request ids are masked in transmission.
[01:22] Marco: how confident are we that this isn't a model OOM or quantization regression? We recently switched to a q4 model variant in the pilot.
[01:35] Devon: good q - we checked model telemetry; no OOMs flagged. The q4 variant has slightly higher tail latencies but nothing that would explain that full spike. The pattern points to concurrency and cache misses.
[01:52] Priya: and our clients' retry policy was naive — they had fixed jitterless retries at 3 attempts with 200ms fixed backoff, which amplified the load.
[02:09] Sofia: that matches what we normally see; the combination of short, synchronized retries plus a token-based rate limit will cause the bucket to drain and then return 429/5xx depending on window.
[02:25] Ethan: can Redwood throttle per-key gracefully? We want per-tenant limits rather than global when possible.
[02:36] Devon: yes - we support per-api-key token buckets and sliding-window quotas. In Hosted mode we have shared pool heuristics; Dedicated gives you more isolation. For the POC we can enable a temporary per-customer hard cap and also a 'soft backpressure' that returns 429 with Retry-After instead of 5xx.
[02:56] Priya: would that require a redeploy or is it a config toggle?
[03:05] Devon: config toggle on our side — low risk. We'll flip soft rate-limits on for TerraScale and add conservative defaults.
[03:21] Marco: and what about circuit-breaker behavior? Something that stops retries from hitting the model if downstream is degraded.
[03:33] Devon: we have circuit-breakers in the runtime. The issue was that clients retried faster than the circuit breaker could trip because of short time windows. So we need to tune both sides: longer initial backoff on client and lower threshold for server-side circuit-break.
[03:52] Sofia: ok let's capture that as an action: Devon will propose server thresholds, Priya will push client backoff changes in the next deployment.
[04:07] Priya: agreed. One more: we saw a KV "cash" miss spike - Devon's term earlier, can you explain? (laughter)
[04:18] Devon: sorry, KV cache — sometimes the transcriber likes 'cash' — we had a miss storm when lots of long-context requests came in and the in-memory K-V cache entries weren't warmed due to sequence sharding. That increased regeneration and compute, raising latencies.
[04:39] Ethan: is that a product limitation for the q4 variant? Could be we changed prompt lengths too.
[04:47] Devon: not variant-specific; it's about session affinity and KV cache partitioning. For small pilots you see this when many concurrent distinct sessions cause low reuse. We recommended enabling prefix caching for repeat prompt segments — we can show config.
[05:03] Marco: any quick mitigation for today?
[05:08] Devon: immediate mitigations: 1) enable soft per-key rate-limits; 2) increase client backoff to exponential (base 300ms, max 5s); 3) enable burst Dedicated capacity if you want a fast safety valve.
[05:26] Sofia: on Dedicated burst: I will send a pricing note, but it's essentially reserved plus a small burst pool we can route to during incidents. That eliminates cross-tenant noise.
[05:38] Priya: what's the lead time for the Dedicated burst? If it's just a toggle we can do it fast, but if we need infra provisioning it's longer.
[05:47] Devon: we can provision a temporary burst within 24-48h in most cases for POCs, but sustained capacity needs a commit. We'll document the exact SLA.
[06:00] Ethan: about observability: we need trace-id propagation examples. Our logs had partial ids so stitching was hard.
[06:11] Devon: noted. We'll add trace-id propagation sample header (x-redwood-trace) and an example in the dashboard. Also add a quick query to find requests that had retry-count >1 and check latencies.
[06:28] Priya: can you also add a synthetic test to hit 1k and 5k RPS patterns? We'll provide the sample shapes.
[06:36] Devon: yes, that's in the sim plan. I'll run a 5k RPS sim with realistic inter-arrival and retries to reproduce the backoff storm.
[06:46] Sofia: quick question — did the token billing impact result in dropped tokens? Priya: you said you saw throttling at the auth layer.
[06:56] Priya: right, we saw some 429s that looked like token exhaustion on the gateway before Redwood admitted requests. We think a misconfigured front proxy was rate-limiting us.
[07:08] Devon: good call to audit the entire path. We'll help triage but that might be on TerraScale infra side.
[07:15] Ethan: yes, we already found a mismatch in our Envoy header logic that caused rate-limit keys to collide. Fixing that reduced some 429s.
[07:25] Marco: let's set success criteria for the next week: 1) sim reproduces <0.5% 5xx at 5k RPS with tuned backoff, 2) dashboards show correct alerts, 3) clients updated with exponential backoff.
[07:43] Sofia: sounds good. Any blockers on the sim data? Priya?
[07:49] Priya: we'll upload traffic CSV by Monday and also indicate peak hour shape.
[07:55] Devon: we've been looking at the request ids in the attached logs — note that some of the latency spikes correlate with model-state fetches due to long context windows; a small prompt-splitting on client side could reduce repeated KV reads.
[08:11] Ethan: could you show a sample refactor of the prompt? That might be a quick win.
[08:17] Devon: yep, we'll add a prompt-splitting example in the repo.
[08:23] Sofia: ok, next, security questions from TerraScale - are there any concerns enabling dedicated burst? Marco?
[08:32] Marco: we just want to ensure data isolation and KMS integration — nothing exotic. Also audit logs preserved.
[08:40] Devon: Dedicated supports VPC peering, KMS, and audit log retention. We'll attach the feature checklist and show options in the Console.
[08:52] Priya: please share the feature checklist.
[08:55] Sofia: I'll send the Dedicated checklist along with pricing by Friday.
[09:02] (crosstalk)
[09:10] Sofia: shifting back — timeline for fixes? Devon, can you propose exact parameter values for server thresholds and backoff?
[09:18] Devon: propose: server circuit-break trip at 60% of token burst for 30s window, return 429 with Retry-After; server-side min retry delay 200ms with 2x exponential; client-side base retry 300ms with jitter, max 5s, max attempts 4. I'll put numbers in the doc.
[09:40] Priya: we'll take that and test; on client side we can get changes into a canary tomorrow.
[09:48] Ethan: for dashboards: add an alert when 5xx rate > 0.3% sustained for 5 minutes and when token-bucket fullness > 80% for 2 out of 3 intervals.
[10:04] Devon: logging advice: include x-redwood-trace, retry-count header, and response latency; we'll give sample logs.
[10:16] Priya: one pain point: the SDK hides some headers — is there an SDK config to propogate trace ids?
[10:25] Devon: yes, in the newer SDK it's opt-in to avoid header leakage. We'll share a small snippet to enable trace propagation.
[10:36] Sofia: great. Any other concerns from the team?
[10:40] Marco: just the economics — if we route to Dedicated burst frequently, what's the expected burn rate? Sofia?
[10:48] Sofia: I'll include cost estimate scenarios in the pricing doc: short bursts are relatively cheap but continuous usage requires reservation. I'll show a per-1k-requests delta.
[10:59] Priya: also, are there any quick fixes to reduce token consumption? We have noisy telemetry that increases token counts for each call.
[11:08] Devon: optimize prompts, use shorter context, leverage embeddings store for static info. We can run a cost-reduction analysis after the sim.
[11:20] Sofia: ok let's recap actions and owners. Devon will run the 5k sim and propose server thresholds; Priya will upload traffic; Ethan will add alerts; Sofia will share pricing and Dedicated checklist. We'll reconvene next week same time to review sim.
[11:40] Priya: thanks, one last question - did Redwood see any internal degradation metrics that correlate with our timestamps?
[11:48] Devon: yes the runtime trace shows higher queue depths in the US-east cluster at the time; we'll attach the graphs to the sheet.
[11:58] Marco: thanks, appreciate the responsiveness.
[12:03] Sofia: thanks all, we'll follow up in the doc and I'll send calendar invite for the canary test. Bye.
